newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ambassadors resume cotton anti-dumping talks.
newsitem.headline: EU ambassadors resume cotton anti-dumping talks.

text.p: European Union member states resumed discussions on Thursday on plans for definitive anti-dumping duties on cotton imports from China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Turkey and Pakistan, diplomats and officials said.

A majority of the 15 EU ambassadors had earlier rejected the European Commission's anti-dumping proposal, diplomats said, meaning the provisional duties on unbleached cotton imports were likely to lapse on their May 20 expiry date.
But a second official said EU ambassadors had returned to fresh proposals later on Thursday, meeting in a restricted session in an attempt to broker a compromise.
"It's not true to say that they have rejected the proposal or rather it's not yet true," the official said.
The Commission imposed provisional duties against grey cotton fabrics from the six named countries last November, setting in train the further review period expiring on May 20.
Renewed discussions indicate that those countries backing duties are trying to patch together a deal before the deadline.
Belgium, Greece, Spain, France, Italy and Portugal supported the proposal earlier on Thursday, two countries shy of the simple majority needed to impose final duties.
